utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let the witness take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you'd like to take a seat.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The pseudonym for this witness will be Witness W.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, there will be a necessary part of the evidence --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: There will be a necessary part of the evidence in private session where potentially identifying answers would be given, but, first of all, can the witness look at this piece of paper. Without reading the name, simply tell us if that is his name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And before we turn to anything else, can you please just, with the assistance of the usher when he's back at the overhead projector, just help us about a few matters of geography.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Apparently we are in private session, in which I can deal with things a little more easily.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a checkpoint between Stupni Do and the village of Mir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: No, there was a checkpoint on the other side of the hill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Facing the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Can we see that, then, best on the map? Just if you can indicate roughly where it was on the map, please. There's a pointer on the desk, if you would like to use that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you point it out on the map that's on the overhead projector, if you can see it? It may be we can get it a tiny bit sharper. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Could you blow it up a little?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you would point it out on the -- yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Just a moment. There, here [indicates]. A checkpoint was here [indicates] and facing the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, in July of 1993, or did people go to that checkpoint to discover that men by the name of Pejcinovic, Duzinovic, Milicevic, and the commander of the Bobovac Brigade, Gavran, were there, and did Duznovic say that the ABiH had to remove the checkpoint and fill in the trenches?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when someone said -- don't say who -- but when somebody said that the trenches were in defence of the Serbs, what did Duznovic say would happen as a result?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: He said, "This enclave," and pointed at the village of Stupni Do, "needs to be burnt, scorched."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to all of you present, was that an obvious threat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the summer of 1993, were some ABiH men from Stupni Do arrested and captured in Vares and kept prisoner there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear of their treatment directly from them or was there a long chain of communication before you learnt what happened to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: I learnt from Mr. Milicevic that they had been arrested and that they were not being treated humanely. It was only later on, after the army entered Vares, I learnt -- I found out what -- everything they had gone through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what treatment -- in a couple of sentences -- did they suffer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: They were beaten. They were all badly battered, were stabbed with knives. The soles of their feet were stabbed. One of them was an invalid, he did not have a leg, and he was beaten with his own leg. Subsequently he was taken to the Swedish battalion, and the others stayed in prison until the army came. And according to their accounts, some 23 of them had been designated for the -- to be put before the firing squad. But they stayed -- because of the army operations, they stayed in prison, and that's where UNPROFOR found them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Paragraph 12 of the summary. Paragraph 11, sorry. Until the end of September, 1993, were you able to travel outside the village to get supplies from humanitarian organisations, but that wasn't possible after September?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Some days before the attack with which we are immediately concerned, did people make efforts, by contacting Milicevic, to get the release of the men who'd been held in Vares and --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- and despite efforts, the men were not released, on the grounds that they were Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes. Not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A couple of days before the attack, the village, fearing danger, was the digging of shelters organised -- don't say by whom -- and were preparations made for medical assistance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 22nd of October of 1993, did you hear rumours? Just yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From whom did you hear those rumours, if you can be specific?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: We heard the rumours on the eve of the attack. We heard those rumours from a neighbour who was a brother -- who was a brother of a man married to a woman of Croat ethnicity. And the rumours were that they had left the village, and that was a sign to us that something was wrong.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that departure of the Croat resident the departure of the only Croat who had until then been living in the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was something also said about the village of Kopljari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes. In the village of Kopljari, a conflict took place between the army and the HVO, and as far as I know, two HVO members were killed and one of them was even buried in the cemetery in the village of Mir, so that we could see that directly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we see Kopljari on our map or not? I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: It's on the other side of the Vares municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: A bit more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'd heard about these deaths in Kopljari. In what way, if at all, did they connect or may they have connected with your fears of what was to happen and indeed what did happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: At some earlier meetings organised by the army and the HVO staff, Chief Pejcinovic threatened that he would attack villages with the Muslim population if the Vares municipality were attacked from any one side by the army. But we already knew that, and that is why I put the two and two together. There Stupni Do might be attacked because it was the nearest and the village itself was surrounded by the Croat population.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If the Chamber is using the larger map, the coloured map, Kopljari is almost due west of Vares, and if looking at the map in my hand, it's a couple of inches to the west. It's not shown on the map on the ELMO at the moment. I think it's necessary to go into private session, if we may, for the next passage of evidence, for, in reality, in a village as small as this, the individual steps taken by an individual person would probably be revealing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know the man Dario Kordic, at any stage of these events, by sight? Just "Yes" or "No".

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that because you knew him personally or because you had seen him on television or his photograph in newspapers? What was the position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: I saw him on television and a few times in Vares.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want you to deal with the times you saw him in Vares. First of all, when did you see him there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: I saw him in Vares at the end of the autumn of 1992. That was the first time. The second time I saw him on the road from the municipal building to the church in Vares. I saw him in the street this other time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the first occasion that you saw him, a quick picture, please: What was he doing? How was he dressed? Who was he with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: The first time I saw him was in front of the municipal building of Vares. Outside there were official cars that were parked, their official cars, and also his escorts were there, like his bodyguards. He wore a camouflage uniform. He had a very short haircut. He wore glasses. I remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise anybody else present at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes. He was with Mr. Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any local residents associated with him or with Blaskic or both of them at that time, or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: No. I only saw them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how was he behaving? How was he apparently being treated by his bodyguards and so on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: They were around him, perhaps five or ten metres away. They were well armed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was Mr. Kordic's apparent attitude and behaviour insofar as you could judge it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: I saw him a few times on television, local television in Vares, because the HVO made it impossible for us to watch TV Bosnia-Herzegovina, because they destroyed one of the transmitters. So we could only watch local television, and Mr. Kordic appeared on TV a few times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: His attitude when you saw him on the street, what was he like then? If you can describe it for us. If not, we'll move to the other visit, the other sighting.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Well, he was not armed. He wore a camouflage uniform. His bodyguards were around him. That's what I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The second sighting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: I saw him in the street, the street that goes from the municipal building of Vares to the Croat church, which is near the municipal building of Vares.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anything special about that occasion? How was he dressed? Was he alone? Was he with anyone else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Again, he wore a camouflage uniform. They were walking towards the road -- towards the church.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have bodyguards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The witness did also lose another family member, but I needn't go into that in detail. It will be covered, I think, in another way. The balance of paragraph 20 I'll deal with through another witness as well. That's all I ask this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Naumovski:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness W, may I introduce my myself. I'm Mitko Naumovski. I'm an attorney at law from Zagreb, and I'm one of the Defence counsels of Mr. Kordic. I am going to put a few questions to you, but I have to tell you something that is customary. Since you and I understand each other as soon as we start speaking, could you please wait a bit until my question is interpreted to you into one of the official languages of the court? Do you understand what I'm saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. W, you made seven statements until now, some of them to the investigators of The Hague Tribunal and others to the police in Sarajevo -- rather, the higher court in Sarajevo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also talked to the Prosecutor during these past few days while you were in The Hague; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Only once, briefly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One of the statements you made was before the higher court in Sarajevo, on the 14th of May, 1996. You were heard as a witness then. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to this file, it seems that you made a witness statement in criminal proceedings against Emir or Emin -- Emin with an "N" -- Crutic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Ermin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He's a Muslim, a Bosniak, as it is called today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes, from a mixed marriage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was one of the suspects from this event that took place in your village; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A few general questions, very briefly. The local commune of Stupni Do is about two kilometres away from the town of Vares; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the photograph that was shown to you, one can see the road that leads to your village; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, can we agree that there is also another road that can be taken to your village, and that is the one through the forest, so to speak, the one that leads to the village of Mir and that also goes to your village too; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: No. No. No. No. No. That is the road that leads to the village of Mir, and it is much farther away. It's ten kilometres farther away, and the locals from Stupni Do don't use that road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The village of Stupni Do, until the 23rd of October, 1993, that is to say, until the events that you told us about, was under Muslim authority. That is to say that it was under the BH army; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes, it was under the BH army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When we look at the entire territory of the administrative borders of the then municipality of Vares, do we agree that one part of the municipality was under the HVO and other parts were under the BH army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned today a Croat. I think his name was Stjepan Miocevic. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Stjepan Milicevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, all right. The transcript said differently. He was coordinator between the residents of Stupni Do and the HVO government in Vares?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this an official capacity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: He was liaison officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to move on to another subject, so I've just looked at my watch. Perhaps it would not be good for me to embark on a new subject altogether now. I have about ten questions with regard to that particular subject. I can say immediately that I do not have too many questions and that we are going to be finished relatively soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We'll adjourn for the usual break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Naumovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness W, may we resume? A few questions with regard to the Territorial Defence or, rather, the BH army unit in your village. Your Honours, perhaps I shall also have to ask to go into private session, because I might -- just to avoid the risk of disclosing anything that could be harmful to the witness. But I think this initial part can be done without it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your village, you had a TO unit which subsequently was renamed the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that in your village, there were about 36 or maybe 37 combatants, that is, soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps we could go into private session now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness W, the BH army unit, did it hold any checkpoints around the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes, facing the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Today you said explicitly that there were no roadblocks between your village and the village of Mir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I must remind you that in one of your statements, you explicitly stated that there was a roadblock between your village and the village of Mir. It is your statement of the 3rd of November. It is when you were referring to the second meeting that took place then, and you said that it took place at the checkpoint manned by Bosnia-Herzegovina between Stupni Do and Mir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes. There was a trench, too, facing the Serbs. But that checkpoint was not preventing the villagers of Mir to pass through normally. Nobody stopped them and nobody laid a finger on them. That is, it was not intended for them but for the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But we do agree that it was there? That was my question. It did exist, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: There was a trench with our members.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I mean a checkpoint. Let us not confuse the trench and the checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's not argue about these matters. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were regularly briefed on the military situation in your village by the president of the war presidency, Mervana Hadzimurtezic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Well, not regularly, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But that is what you said in your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Well, we did keep in touch perhaps once a month, we had contact, because we had to walk 20 -- 28 kilometres to reach the Vares municipal authority, which had been dislocated, and it was very difficult because one had to go beneath the Serb lines and it involved a major risk. I mean, it was really very hazardous to go there, so we met once a month.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand, but I also meant contact by radio.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One question relative to those six arrested soldiers who were captured at Pajto Han, if I understood you properly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those soldiers were captured at the time when -- around the villages of Mir, Jankovici and Dragojlovice. Fighting was going on between the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, coming from the direction of Kakanj and the HVO; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And a few short questions with regard to those two meetings you had with the HVO representatives?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: At the first meeting on the 21st of June, 1993, the HVO requested from you to lay down your weapons, and they put the same request to the village Dastansko a few days before that; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did you not lay down your weapons, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And nothing happened? There was no reaction to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Well, we were threatened, actually. We were threatened that the village would be attacked unless we surrendered our weapons by the morning. That was a verbal threat from the then chief, Pejcinovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, but I went a step further. What I meant was that although you did not lay down your weapons, that village was not attacked and nothing happened.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yeah, but meanwhile a letter arrived from Visoko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You already told us about that. Thank you. But otherwise we're referring to this period of time. Another question: There were quite a number of refugees and ex-police from Kakanj, Sipidsko [phoen], or something like that. There were about 15 to 20,000 people who had come to the municipality of Vares, isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just one question related to the strategic position of your village, strategic location of your village. The HVO held Perun, where this transmitter was that you mentioned, and the road to Perun was controlled by you, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But didn't you control that road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. At the second meeting on the 31st of July, 1993, you were told that the roadblock had to be lifted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: We were told that everything had to be removed, not only the checkpoint. The "checkpoint," I don't know what you mean by that, but there was a trench with some three or four soldiers who were there on night guard, because in the vicinity of that place was an intersection, and we simply were afraid of the incursion of Serb forces from another hill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I am getting your meaning, you were asked to remove that checkpoint and shovel the earth in to close the trench?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes. They asked us to close the trench and to remove our men who were around the village; that is, we were told that all soldiers should go back to their homes so that they should take over the complete control and that nobody would lay a finger on us. But remembering what happened before, we did not and we really could not agree to that. Because all of those who had laid their weapons, I mean, we know what happened to them. Most of them were slain and their houses burnt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But, Witness W, that is not what happened to the village of Dastansko, rather, the population?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Its population, yes, but that is because they fled to another village. The whole village fled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness W, let us move on to the incident on the 23rd of October, because I have a few questions about that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understood you well, on the basis of accounts which reached you from Vares, you concluded that there would be a retaliatory action because of the victory won in the village of Kopljari by the army of BH when the 20 Croat soldiers were killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Not 20. I know about two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I may, I think this figure, which says "20" or, rather, about 20 -- "20-odd," in the first statement that you gave to the security services centre in Sarajevo on the 27th of October, 1993, which you signed to.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: That is a mistake.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it is -- it is written out: "20-odd." So it is not a figure. You think it is a mistake?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The witness has explained the mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is also the information that a Croat came to fetch his sister living in your village. A Croat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: No, the brother. The brother of our neighbour who was a Croat woman. He came at dusk, before the nightfall, and took away the whole family in a direction which we did not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. That is what I was going to say. And you concluded from that something was about to happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: I concluded that something was wrong, because the gentleman who was married to that Croat woman was a member of our civilian village committee, and I concluded that something was wrong.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the council of your neighbourhood community met, and you decided that the whole population should be mobilised; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that the village defence had to be prepared to defend the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: In cooperation with the unit commander, naturally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was the commander? If you can tell us that without disclosing anything, since we're in open session, without disclosing your identity. Can you tell us or not? Was it a cousin of yours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: No. It was Mr. Likic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of those preparations, you dug out some shelters under the ground, you dug trenches. Perhaps some of them already existed there before.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then the fire brigade had some drills and you also received some training in the extension of first-aid, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Well, yes, but that meant sand and water around houses, as much as we could do, and that was something that already existed before. What we did that evening was merely to do around, check it, perhaps add something here or there, because there was little time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were ready for a possible attack, the attack that you thought might come?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: I can tell you candidly that after the first ultimatum, we did not really think it would happen, but we could expect it. But, you know, subconsciously we thought they would not attack us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you used that word that you were ready; that you were prepared; that you had undertaken all the necessary preparations.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes, we had done that, but that such an attack would take place and with so many people and it would be so fierce that it would be wholesale slaughter, that is something that we did not think possible at all, let alone happening to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness W, you personally, using communications devices, notified the staff of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina about a possible attack. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: No. No, sir, I did not. I could not keep in touch with them. I could only listen to the radio, but it was -- the radio was manned by the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. But what I told you, the witness, and I won't repeat his name, the one that I referred to beforehand, he said that you reported to the staff of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina using the radio.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Sir, your witness was not there. Your witness was 30 kilometres away in the town of Breza.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right, but wouldn't you agree with me that the war presidency in Dabravine, with the president Mervana Hadzemurtezic, decided civilians from your village should be evacuated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes. The first time, yes. The first time of when we received the ultimatum, rather, when Pejcinovic threatened that they would attack, and we did that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And perhaps I was not clear enough, Witness W. I meant the decision of the 22nd of October, 1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. The villages were evacuated then, but some 7 or 15 days later -- no. Sorry. I think we're talking about cross-purposes. I'm referring to the day preceding the attack, not the other event. So I shall repeat my question. Would you agree with me that the war presidency, on the 22nd of October, 1993, decided that the civilians should be evacuated from the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that the army should just stay behind and defend the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I must again tell you that this witness whom I mentioned before said that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I'm going to stop you, because all you're doing is asking the witness to comment on what another witness has said. I haven't stopped you so far, but this witness's answer has been that the other witness wasn't there. The right way, if I may say so, to deal with this is for you to comment at the end, when you have your chance to make your submissions, about any differences there may be. What we have to deal with is this witness's evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, all I wanted to do was, following your earlier instructions, I simply wanted to confirm the witness with a set of facts. But if you think this is not the time for it, then I shall move on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To conclude this subject, you did not receive any order from the war presidency with regard to events that would probably ensue in -- that is, I mean the order on the 22nd of October, '93?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As for this event, you already told us which units took part in the attack on your village, because you heard accounts about that from Vares inhabitants?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness W, you have given seven statements so far, plus the interview with the Prosecutor which we see recorded in this outline that we received before your testimony, and nowhere -- not one of those documents mentions what you said today, and that is that one of the units participating in this incident came from Busovaca. Could you answer, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: I don't understand you. All those places are very close to one another, and I did not think it necessary to list all the small and large localities because Kresevo, Kiseljak, and Busovaca are very near and all those guys come from those -- from that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, but Busovaca was cut off from Kiseljak, and the Court knows that, and that happened a long time before that event.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So may I ask the witness to read to us what he said to the judge at the Supreme Court in Sarajevo when he was testifying about these circumstances, just one sentence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Is the point that he did not mention Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely, Your Honours. It says the same thing as the outline which we were given today, and it is very short. If I may, I shall read it myself, if you prefer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, and then ask the witness if he has any comment to make.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So I'm quoting. This is a statement. It doesn't have the date, but I believe we agree with the Prosecution it was the 1st of August, 1996. I'm quoting: "That morning when I was in Stupni Do, I am well aware that all formations of the HVO from the territory of the municipality of Vares participated in it and that soldiers from the municipality of Kiseljak, then Apostoli, Maturice took part in it," end of quotation marks, "and some units from Kakanj." So wouldn't you agree with me that you were instructed by the investigating magistrate that you had to tell the truth, that you should not conceal anything, and so on and so forth, and that you sign this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you did not mention any other municipality, but the most thing of all is that you mentioned the names of the units which did indeed come from the Kiseljak municipality, and that is Maturice and Apostoli?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So are we agreed that after so many years after the event, you mentioned Busovaca for the first time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: I'm only repeating that all these places are one next to the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't want the Court to tell me that I'm ranting, but between Busovaca and Kiseljak are the troops of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. But it is up to the Court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very briefly, as briefly as possible about Mr. Dario Kordic, today you mentioned when you first saw Mr. Kordic in Vares approximately, but when did you see him the second time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: You're asking for the date or what?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the part of year, whatever.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember, but I remember seeing him twice. It's been five or six years, after all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that the first time, it was towards the end of the autumn. However, this other event that you described, in terms of going to the church, could have been and was on the 29th of September, when the Catholics celebrate Saint Mihovil, their patron saint, in Vares?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: I don't know. You probably know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I said this in order to jog your memory. Perhaps can you remember now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: No, no, no, no, no. No, no, no, I do not remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, could we have this for the transcript? It was on the 29th of September, 1992. Perhaps I did not mention it specifically. Perhaps it's been my mistake.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then Mr. Kordic gave an interview on television. Maybe you saw it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: I do not recall. I saw Mr. Kordic on television a few times -- not once only; several times -- on the local television in Vares.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't have to put any other questions to this witness. I just wish to recall my answer in response to your question, Your Honour. On page 3.402, when I explicitly said that Mr. Kordic was in Vares only in order to celebrate the patron saint of Vares, Saint Mihovil, on the 29th and perhaps the 30th of September, 1992, but it was one single visit, and perhaps I can add this was not in the company of General Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for your patience, and I would conclude my questioning with this, and I wish to thank the witness as well. Re-examined by Mr. Nice:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just two things: refugees and movements of people in and out of Vares. You've spoken of the number of incoming people to Vares. When was that and where were they coming from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Are you asking me, sir?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I am. Sorry, my mistake. Yes. Can you help us with people coming into Vares, when and where they were coming from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Could you please clarify that, because refugees were coming to Vares from all parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, then I'm going to take it short -- sorry. I'm going to take it shortly, and if this question doesn't prompt an immediate answer, I'll move on. Did the incoming refugees have any effect on the departure of Croats from Vares at any time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. The second point: Busovaca. Had you, in fact, mentioned Busovaca to the Office of the Prosecutor in the proofing sessions you've had here this week?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How clear or with what degree of certainty do you recall being informed that Busovaca was one of the named municipalities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: Immediately, as soon as the army entered Vares, and upon the release of the prisoners from the high school in Vares, many people said where these young men came from. Kakanj was mentioned, Busovaca was mentioned, Kresevo was mentioned, Kiseljak was mentioned. Kiseljak was mentioned as the main centre, the main recruitment centre for these paramilitary units.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I hope the Chamber will take it from me that the --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W
utterances.text: That is why I thought that Kiseljak was the most important.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you. I hope the Chamber will take it from me that the summary was deficient, and it was my oversight and it should have been put right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Anything else?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Nothing else for this witness, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm not sure, but should we just, for the record, say that we don't have a cross, because this witness is clearly not related to any counts for which Mr. Cerkez is indicted for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Will that go for the next witness too?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Witness W, thank you for coming to the International Tribunal. Your evidence is now concluded. You are released, and, as I say, thank you very much for coming.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too, Sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: While the Chamber is being adjusted for the departure of the witness and the arrival of the next witness, may exhibits of this witness, I think really all, be kept under seal, except for the photographs, for reasons of potential identification?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: While the witnesses are changing over, can I make this observation briefly? I heard, of course, the exchange between Your Honour and Mr. Naumovski about his not being allowed to put something that emerged from another witness and his reference to an earlier ruling of the Chamber. That, of course, is a ruling that a positive case has got to be put, or perhaps in certain circumstances is properly put, which is different from putting the evidence of another witness. And I simply observe that for my part; I'm not following what is the case on Stupni Do. I don't imagine it's being advanced that this was in any way a lawful retaliation, but for my part, in case it's material, I don't follow what's being put. I will attempt to deal with the next witness swiftly. She covers different ground. But if I'm going to be allowed to lead most of it, then I hope we may conclude her by the luncheon adjournment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. In general, even not in particular, it's corroborative evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: It is, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Is there any objection to some leading? Anything which shouldn't be led?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely no objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let the witness take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The pseudonym for this witness will be Witness X. Examined by Mr. Nice:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness X, can you look, please, at this piece of paper? Just confirm by the answer "Yes" that this is your name, but don't read the name out.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you living in Stupni Do with your family in 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was the one woman named Ana Likic who was a Croat --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- but married to a Muslim. Was --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All other villages in your immediate area were Bosnian Croat villages?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, of course, your village was near, in 1993, October, was near to the confrontation lines with the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately how many villagers were allocated to defending the village from attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: Perhaps between 30 and 40.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did some of them have rifles and uniforms, but did they mostly operate in civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there some trenches which had been there for some time, notably from the time when the HVO and the ABiH had cooperated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was life comparatively normal until August '93, when the HVO representatives came to your village, presenting an ultimatum that people should surrender their weapons to the control of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From this time on, the ultimatum being refused, from this time on when people from Stupni Do went to Vares, were they treated badly sometimes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were some imprisoned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were some the subject of, effectively, theft?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever dealt with personally in this way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you have taken from you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: The food supplies I had bought.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was it that they took food supplies from you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: In Vares Majden. At their place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Explain that. Is that on the way up to Stupni Do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes. On the road towards Stupni Do. From Vares Majden towards Stupni Do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many times did you have food supplies taken from you? Once or more than once?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: Several times. And they also didn't let us go into town. They would make us turn back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able also, if asked, to say -- to talk about similar events happening to Dervis Mahmutovic and Resad Likic, who had his car taken, as well as his money?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the ultimatum, villagers left the village, fearing an attack, but returned, and things were relatively quiet until the 23rd of October.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Although there had been some increase in HVO patrols.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then on the 22nd of October, I should have said, the only Croat was taken away by her brother, along with her husband, and that caused alarm in the village.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You heard shooting on the morning of the 23rd. It's not challenged, I think, that that shooting came from Vares, Mir, Bijelo Borje, and Vares Majden?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: Bijelo Borje, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to a shelter with your sons while your husband --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Was there indeed an arrangement that several families would meet in this particular shelter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in due course, did other families arrive so that there was a total of some nine adults and six children in the shelter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After an hour, did you return -- or thereabouts, did you return from the shelter to your house to get shoes for your sons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time did you then have a view of the damage already done to the village and did you see several houses on fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember now whose houses were on fire at that stage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: Melca Beganovic, Halid Likic, Serif Likic, as far as I could see, those houses. And also Mlado Orozovic house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your house was itself destroyed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And indeed in the attack overall, every house except one was destroyed, I think.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you returned to the shelter, did you receive advice from your husband that the village could not be defended and that the HVO soldiers had effectively broken all lines of defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you try to leave the basement, but at that stage only one adult --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- and two children were able to get out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: Two persons and a child.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the shelter were you able to hear what the soldiers were doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in summary, without, I hope, distressing yourself, just tell us what you could hear.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: The door was open. They were yelling, hollering, shooting. They did all sorts of things in the yard. The door of the shelter was open. We heard them upstairs shooting all over the village. They were upstairs where I had lived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see the soldiers sufficiently to be able to give us a proximate idea of how many there were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: Yes, I saw them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: There were about 15 of them, perhaps even more. I was so afraid that I couldn't even watch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were they dressed and what did they have on their faces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: Their faces were painted black. They had camouflage uniforms. They also had black ribbons round their heads. They had gloves with the fingers cut open and boots and weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they have any patches and did they have any other identifying materials on them, for example, on their arms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: They had white patches and emblems with the letter "U" and also the chessboard sign, and it was very difficult for me to notice anything since I was so frightened.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Unless there is any objection at paragraph 31, I'll put to the witness the first word on the third line in case it jogs her memory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see anything of any ribbons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: On their arms. They had white ribbons on their arms, tied around their arms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. What armament did they have with them, what arms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: They had rifles, different weapons. They shot from all sorts of weapons. They had 84s. They also had bandoliers across their chests.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you speak to any of them? Did any of them speak to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: No. They were only swearing and shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At some stage -- just yes or no to this -- did you learn of what group these men were soldiers? Just yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you learn that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: We learned that when we got out to -- we were told two days later by other people who had found out who they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they, the soldiers themselves, say anything to you or say anything out loud, indicating what group they came from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: Well, they were cursing our balija mothers. They were swearing at everything that belonged to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they themselves identify what groups they came from, group or groups they came from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: No. We didn't hear anything, but we were so frightened that we could not have understood anything. We were trembling with fear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you did hear, some days later, what group they were from, and you heard this from other people, what name of band or group was given as the group of which these soldiers were members?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X
utterances.text: Maturica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of this day, was a girl, a young girl --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, for reasons of general sensitivity, I'm going to ask that this be dealt with in private session, in view of the content of paragraph 36. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: 1 p.m., to be reconvened on Friday, the 3rd day of December, 1999, at 9.30 a.m.
